tn_vapor_lock_cave.blurb: Vapor Lock Cave is a steep, roofed boulder cluster on the hillside above the river in the Dayton Pocket and Laurel-Snow area, north of Chattanooga. The sandstone here is shaped into big horizontal overhangs with pockets, pinches and flakes, and the problems are powerful and sustained. This is a hard-leaning zone: most problems sit at V5 and above, with a heavy cluster from V9 to V11 and a few harder still. The slope faces south, so it picks up sun, and the rock is reported to stay dry in light rain. It is a good place to head when other boulder fields are busy.

tn_y_12.blurb: Y-12 is a steep, shaded sandstone wall in the Clear Creek part of the Obed, home to tall routes and big roofs. It is almost all sport climbing, with a few trad lines, and the grades lean hard: mostly 5.10 through 5.12, with a handful of 5.13s and very little below 5.10. Bring a full set of quickdraws and a stick clip, since first bolts can be high. The shade makes it a comfortable choice when other Obed walls are baking, and the overhanging angle gives it some tolerance for wet weather. The final stretch of the approach uses a wooden ladder, and the turn onto the trail is easy to miss.

tn_stone_fort_bouldering_climbs.blurb: Stone Fort, also known as Little Rock City, is one of the Southeast's best-known sandstone bouldering areas, on Mowbray Mountain about half an hour from Chattanooga. The boulders sit in a compact wooded stretch beside a golf course, so walking between problems is quick. The grades here run from VB up through the V7 range, with most problems between V0 and V7 and a lone V9 at the top end, making it friendly to a wide mix of climbers. It hosts a long-running fall bouldering competition, and cooler months bring the best friction and the biggest crowds.

tn_4_paradise_wall.blurb: Paradise Wall is a section of the Tennessee Wall, the long hard-sandstone cliff above the Tennessee River Gorge near Chattanooga. The routes here are mostly traditional lines, with a smaller group of bolted sport climbs and a single aid line. Grades span 5.7 to the 5.12 and 5.13 range, but the weight sits between 5.10 and 5.12. The wall catches strong sun, so it is a favored cold-weather spot and gets very hot in summer; autumn through spring is the comfortable window.

tn_ijams_crag.blurb: Ijams Crag is a small sport cliff in an old marble and limestone quarry in South Knoxville's Urban Wilderness, about ten minutes from downtown. The walls are short, roughly 30 to 60 feet, and the bolted routes cover beginner terrain up to the 5.13 range, though most fall between 5.10 and 5.12. The face points east-northeast, giving morning sun and shade later in the day. It works well for an after-work session or for newer sport climbers, and the loose rock has largely been cleaned off.
tn_ijams_crag.parking_note: Head for the Aberdeen Lane trailhead in South Knoxville and leave the car on the gravel just inside the first gate.
tn_ijams_crag.approach: From the trailhead, follow Imerys Trail, then bear right onto Burnett Ridge Trail and climb for a couple of minutes to the crag sign, where a right turn leads to the wall.

tn_tieranny_roofs.blurb: Tieranny Roofs is a steep, south-facing sandstone wall on the Clear Creek side of the Obed, capped by a huge roof. It holds some of the longest routes in the Obed and almost all of them are bolted sport lines. Grades start around 5.10 on the slabbier face below the roof and build to the 5.13 range, with the bulk of the climbs between 5.11 and 5.13. Winter sun makes it a good cold-day choice. Bring a 60 m rope and a stick clip. The walk in is long and includes a steep descent with a short scramble, so allow plenty of time.

tn_5_the_wasteland.blurb: The Wasteland is a section of the Tennessee Wall, the hard sandstone cliff overlooking the Tennessee River Gorge near Chattanooga. Every line here is traditional, so expect to place your own gear. The grades cluster firmly in the 5.10 and 5.11 range, with a handful of 5.12s and a few easier lines, making it a good stop for solid intermediate leaders. The cliff soaks up sun, which makes it a cold-weather favorite and a poor idea on hot summer days; the best conditions come from autumn into spring.

tn_buffet_wall.blurb: Buffet Wall is the showpiece sector of Denny Cove, in the Denny East section of South Cumberland State Park. It is a long, steep sandstone wall of sport routes, with sidepull shelves, crimpy seams and a capstone roof overhead. This is a hard wall: nearly everything is 5.11 or tougher, with the densest group at 5.12 and a good number of 5.13s plus a few 5.14s. In winter the sun reaches it most of the day, and in summer it picks up afternoon shade. The approach is a short hike up the main trail.

tn_north_chick_gorge_soddy_tn.blurb: North Chick Gorge lies along North Chickamauga Creek near Soddy-Daisy, a short drive north of Chattanooga, and is better known locally for its swimming hole and whitewater than for climbing. The climbing is a mix of sport routes and boulder problems, with a couple of trad and aid lines. Sport grades mostly fall between 5.11 and 5.13, and the boulders run from VB to V10. Quality varies from crumbly to excellent, and getting to the climbs often takes an adventurous hike over rocky terrain and creek crossings, so wear sturdy shoes and travel with care.

tn_roadside_wall_2.blurb: Roadside Wall is the most popular cliff in Suck Creek Canyon, just outside Chattanooga, and is the usual first stop for newcomers. It mixes traditional lines with a smaller number of sport routes, and the grades run from about 5.7 to 5.12, centered on 5.9 to 5.11. The approach is short but involves a creek crossing with no bridge, so be ready to hop rocks. Suck Creek is quieter than the Tennessee Wall, though the rock is less consistent, so expect an occasional loose or rotten section.
